title: Two lions at watch
material: oil on canvas laid down on board
description: Artist Name: Wilhelm Friedrich Kuhnert | Artwork Title: Two lions at watch | Lot Info: (German, 1865-1926) | Two lions at watch signed 'Wilh. Kuhnert' (lower left) oil on canvas laid down on board 86 x 64cm (33 7/8 x 25 3/16in).
provenance: Acquired directly from the artist. | Private American collection. | Property of a Gentleman. | | The present composition, painted circa 1917, revisits an earlier work completed during Wilhelm Kuhnert's second expedition to Africa in 1905. While both compositions share similarities, Two lions at watch is notably larger and places greater emphasis on the two lions, positioning them as the central figures within the vast African environment. Kuhnert embarked on his first journey to Africa in 1891, he was then commissioned to visit the German and English colonial territories of East and South Africa on safari in 1905 and 1911-12 after gaining popularity. His portrayals of African wildlife, inspired by renowned German animal painter Richard Friese, depict wild animals in their natural settings. Lions held a special significance for Kuhnert, earning him the nickname "Lion-Kuhnert" for his exceptional affinity with the species. | | The authenticity of this work has been previously confirmed by Dr Angelika Grettmann-Werner and is registered in the catalogue raisonné no. 4028.

title: The mermaid
description: Artist Name: John Young Hunter | Artwork Title: The mermaid | Lot Info: (British, 1874-1955) | The mermaid signed 'J.Hunter' (lower right) oil on canvas 41 x 20.5cm (16 1/8 x 8 1/16in).
provenance: With Whitford and Hughes, London. | Private collection, UK. |  | John Young Hunter was born into an artistic family, the son of painter Colin Hunter and the first husband of fellow artist Mary Young Hunter. Their lives were marked by privileged connections to leading figures of the Victorian art world, including John Singer Sargent and Edwin Austin Abbey. Born in Glasgow, Hunter trained at the Royal Academy in London, a decision made by his father who preferred it over the Parisian academies. Together, John and Mary travelled extensively throughout Europe, immersing themselves in various cultures. Initially influenced by the Pre-Raphaelites and his mentors, such as Sargent and Lawrence Alma-Tadema, Hunter became associated with the new Pre-Raphaelite movement. Over time, he shifted his focus towards portraiture, a genre preferred by his patrons. After living for several years in Suffolk, the couple moved to North America, joining prominent art colonies in the western United States. They eventually settled in Taos, New Mexico, where they spent the remainder of their lives and where Hunter passed away in 1955.  | In this evocative work, Hunter explores the timeless subject of the mermaid. This subject, used by several Pre-Raphaelite artists such as John William Waterhouse, often explores the themes of beauty, danger and mystery. Floating beneath the water and surrounded by fish, the figure conveys both serenity and intrigue.  |
